rationale: Start with a broad, moderately fast gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in subsequent injections.

Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to probe selectivity in the crowded middle cluster. All compounds already elute comfortably before 10 minutes, so resolving the critical pairs is the priority.

A shallower gradient at the best temperature should improve separation of the remaining critical pair. The current last peak at 6.58 minutes leaves room to increase gradient duration while aiming to keep all peaks within 10 minutes.

Test an intermediate slope to balance the two critical separations: the longer gradient improved the earlier pair but slightly weakened the later pair. A 12-minute gradient may resolve both while keeping the last peak well below 10 minutes.
The maximum CRF is already achieved; retain injection 4 as the benchmark. Raise temperature one step to test whether elution can be accelerated without losing full resolution.

Return to the successful temperature and raise the starting organic fraction one step to seek earlier elution. This tests whether the slightly shallower gradient can preserve both critical separations while shortening the observed elution window.

The local attempts to accelerate injection 4 lost resolution, so retain it as the maximum-score benchmark. Test a cooler, steeper gradient to look for an alternative selectivity pattern that permits full resolution in less time.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to test whether the remaining middle-pair separation improves while maintaining the fast elution window. Watch the first pair closely, since higher starting organic may compromise its resolution.

Keep the two maximum-score methods as benchmarks and test whether a higher starting organic fraction improves the crowded cluster at 40 C. This explores an alternative selectivity regime that could allow full resolution with earlier final elution.

Back off one endpoint step from injection 19 to restore the successful slope of injection 4 with a shorter programmed gradient. Since the final peak previously eluted before this gradient ends, full resolution and CRF 1.000 are expected without extending the elution window.
